svg.title: Four Gates Before Signing a PBM Contract
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-pbm-contract-gates; chapter number: 5; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Gates Before Signing a PBM Contract; subtitle: Following the money from plan-billed price to retained rebate; caption: Each gate targets a gap the buyer never sees, from AWP-only invoices to narrowed rebate definitions and trade-secret pricing clauses.; assumptions note: Gate order is editorial. Carving out the PBM is available to self-funded sponsors only, since fully insured plans are locked to the carrier's PBM.; note: Sources are RxPreferred, Dr. Eric Bricker of AHealthcareZ - Healthcare Finance Explained, Desai of the American Health Law Association, and Tyler Dutchover.; nodes: gate: G1; question: Does every claim show the pharmacy-paid amount next to the plan-billed amount?; pass next: G2; fail action: Reject AWP-only invoicing. RxPreferred's case paid the pharmacy $10, invoiced $100 plus a $2 admin fee, and kept $92.; gate: G2; question: Will the PBM disclose any customer besides the health plan, plus market share and bonus payments?; pass next: G3; fail action: Demand formulary, market share, and bonus payment disclosure, not just rebates.; gate: G3; question: Does the rebate definition include all discounts and amounts based on a percentage of drug cost?; pass next: G4; fail action: Rewrite the definition, since a narrowed rebate creates revenue pockets outside pass-through.; gate: G4; question: Is the contract free of any clause calling real drug costs confidential trade secrets?; pass next: Sign and carve the PBM out of the carrier bundle if self-funded; fail action: Strike the clause, and assume overpayment if the PBM refuses to show receipts.

text.title: Four Gates Before Signing a PBM Contract
text.tspan: Four Gates Before Signing a PBM Contract

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Does every claim show the pharmacy-paid amount next to the plan-billed amount?; pass next: G2; fail action: Reject AWP-only invoicing. RxPreferred's case paid the pharmacy $10, invoiced $100 plus a $2 admin fee, and kept $92.

gate: G2; question: Will the PBM disclose any customer besides the health plan, plus market share and bonus payments?; pass next: G3; fail action: Demand formulary, market share, and bonus payment disclosure, not just rebates.

gate: G3; question: Does the rebate definition include all discounts and amounts based on a percentage of drug cost?; pass next: G4; fail action: Rewrite the definition, since a narrowed rebate creates revenue pockets outside pass-through.

gate: G4; question: Is the contract free of any clause calling real drug costs confidential trade secrets?; pass next: Sign and carve the PBM out of the carrier bundle if self-funded; fail action: Strike the clause, and assume overpayment if the PBM refuses to show receipts.

text.title: Assumptions: Gate order is editorial. Carving out the PBM is available to self-funded sponsors only, since fully insured plans are locked to the carrier's PBM.
